payload.summary: Reject the direct filter-media de-scaling change and the speculative habitat-weighted shading tweak. Accept the amendments that preserve the happy-path plant-growth guard and the one that identifies the missing scenario/startup parameterization for filter media area.

votes.rationale: The maturity stall is real, but removing geometry scaling is not a complete fix. `FilterHardware::default()` hard-codes 2000 cm² and neither `ScenarioPreset` nor `StartupOverrides` can supply `media_area_cm2`, so this change would make every seeded tank inherit the same filter-media area and just replace one implicit derivation with another incorrect default.

Habitat light is already habitat-specific in the registry: glass, plant surfaces, and substrate each apply different crowding attenuation before `algae_growth.rs` sees `light_exposure`. Adding another habitat-weighted plant-shading layer here is not a demonstrated bug fix and risks double-counting crowding without a failing case or calibration target.

The failing behavior points to the startup biomass assumption, not the test contract. On `medium_planted`, `build_plant_guilds()` with the old 6.0 g/1000 cm² density seeds 21.6 g total biomass across two guilds, and the happy-path test then drops to about 19.2 g after 30 days, so the constant/self-shading model should be validated or retuned before weakening the assertion.

This identifies a real hole in the current filter-media change. Once `scale_hardware_to_geometry()` stops setting `media_area_cm2`, every seeded scenario falls back to the same 2000 cm² default even though flow still scales with volume, and that directly changes habitat area and nitrifier carrying capacity with no way for scenarios or startup overrides to author the hardware.

The test name and doc comment still promise growth under good conditions, so changing it to an 80% survivability check hides a user-visible regression instead of fixing it. That weakens end-to-end coverage exactly where the suite should catch plant decline in a happy-path scenario.
